title: Call-path scenario inventory and prompting notes
summary: Working scrapbook for building a compact inventory of user-facing call-path scenarios, paired prompt sets, and a lightweight eval protocol for onboarding models into the tool-use/function-calling surface. Focused on multi-step flows, ambiguous tool selection, and argument parsing edge cases.
background: We need a repeatable set of scenarios that surface: (1) wrong-tool selection from ambiguous intent, (2) argument mangling when prompts contain nested lists/escaped characters, (3) multi-step tool handoffs where intermediate tool outputs become subsequent tool args, and (4) failure modes under truncation or latency-induced fallback. This doc collects candidate scenarios and prompts for quick integration into the QA harness.
goals: Create 30–40 compact scenarios covering common and adversarial tool-use paths
Produce 3 prompt variants per scenario (short user, contextualized system, noisy user)
Define a minimal rubric for selection correctness, arg fidelity, and flow continuity
Ship a smoke regression suite that runs in < 5 minutes against a local test model build
scope: Surface-level scenarios for onboarding (not long-running orchestration). Prioritize tool selection + argument extraction + multi-call chaining (<4 steps). Exclude persistent user auth workflows and heavy external network pulls.
evaluation_matrix: Header: scenario_id | intent_brief | input_complexity | expected_tool(s) | arg_parse_required | max_steps | priority
S001 | convert-currency request with locale notes | low | currency-converter | yes | 1 | P1
S002 | schedule-meeting with relative dates ("next tuesday") | medium | calendar-create | yes (date resolver) | 1 | P1
S003 | chained recipe: generate shopping list -> find nearest store -> order items | high | list-gen, geo-lookup, order-api | yes (structured items) | 3 | P1
S004 | ambiguous contact lookup (first name only) | medium | contact-search OR ask-clarify | yes | 1 | P2
S005 | math-in-text: parse embedded LaTeX-ish expression for compute | medium | math-eval | yes (expr extraction) | 1 | P2
S006 | code-exec sandbox: provide code, ask for output and explanation | high | code-run, explain | yes (code blob) | 2 | P2
prompt_sets: Short-user: "Book a table for 2 at a sushi spot near my office tomorrow evening. Use local timezone."

Contextualized-system: "You are an assistant with access to tools: calendar-create(date, time, attendees, locale), restaurant-search(location, cuisine, radius). Prefer explicit confirmations for ambiguous requests."
Noisy-user: "hey can u pls book smth? sushi near 94107 maybe 7pm? my timezone PST? tnx"
Adversarial: "Schedule a meeting next month on the 31st and charge the attendee list to account 'X'; include note: 'confirm@@@'"
Structured-instruction: "Return JSON only: {tool: <name>, args: {}}. For ambiguous fields set 'needs_clarification': true."
Tool-fallback hint: "If the restaurant search returns >3 matches prioritize ratings >4.3 and delivery unavailable."
scenario_samples: S003-detailed: User: "I want dinner for 6; give me a shopping list for a paella, find a grocery within 2 miles that has saffron, then place an order." Expected: list-gen -> geo-lookup(query: saffron) -> order-api(items:list) ; Validate: item names preserved, quantities numeric, store availability flag.

S004-edge: User: "Call Jordan and tell them the event is moved." Context: Contacts contain Jordan Lee (mobile), Jordan Patel (work) and 'Jordan' ambiguous. Expected: assistant should request clarification or pick with high recency score; if picks, provide evidence (last contact date).
S002-relative-date: User: "Can we meet 'this Friday' about the Q3 deck?" Expect date-resolved based on user's locale; verify timezone propagation to calendar-create args.
Arg-escaping: Prompt contains JSON blob inside text (nested braces). Ensure parser extracts the JSON and passes it verbatim to the appropriate tool without trimming escape sequences.

Multi-step failure recovery: Agent attempts tool A -> tool B fails with 503 -> agent retries A with modified args or falls back to alternative tool C. Check retry counts and fallback rationale in logs.
test_protocol: 1) Seed harness loads scenario Sx and three prompt variants. 2) Send prompts to model under test with function-calling enabled and capture selected tool name(s), full args, tokens, and streaming events. 3) Run lightweight validator: check tool selection match against expected_tool(s) (soft match allowed for alternatives), run schema check on args (presence/format of required fields), and run flow continuity: for chains, verify output of step N used as input to N+1 with <=20% token mutation. 4) If any check fails, capture full model response + raw tokens and tag with failure reason. 5) Aggregate metrics across scenarios and compare to previous baseline to detect regressions.
metrics: tool_selection_accuracy: percent of responses that chose an expected tool or acceptable alternative
arg_fidelity_score: percent of required argument fields preserved and formatted correctly
chain_continuity: percent of chains where downstream steps consumed upstream outputs without manual correction
clarification_rate: percent of ambiguous requests where model asked for a clarification
fallback_rate: percent of attempts that used fallback tools or retries
regression_alert: binary flag if delta(tool_selection_accuracy) < -3% vs baseline
observed_risk_modes: hallucinated_tool: model invents a tool name not in the manifest
argument_truncation: long lists truncated and result in missing items
type_coercion_error: numeric strings passed where ints expected ("3" vs 3)
fallback_oscillation: model flips between tool A and B across retries
privacy_leakage: model includes PII from context in tool args unintentionally
quick_notes:
- Preference for JSON-only validator output when running automated checks.
- Use small synthetic contact list and grocery inventory snapshots to make tests deterministic.
- Keep one noisy-wire test per scenario to catch tokenization issues.
- TODO: add canonical examples for locale edge cases (non-Gregorian dates).
execution_plan_and_timeline: Phase 0 (1 week): curate 20 core scenarios + 3 prompts each. Phase 1 (2 weeks): implement validators and CI hook (smoke run). Phase 2 (ongoing): expand to 50 scenarios and add heavy adversarial set. Owners: Maya (coord), Liam (validator impl), Diego (CI).
